title: Particle Filter SLAM on KITTI LiDAR
subtitle: Coursework implementation of particle-filter SLAM with occupancy grid mapping
summary: Implemented a Rao-Blackwellized particle filter SLAM pipeline on KITTI LiDAR, including SE(2) motion propagation, log-odds occupancy mapping, stratified resampling, and numerically stable weight updates.

glance.oneLiner: Rao-Blackwellized particle-filter SLAM on KITTI LiDAR with log-odds occupancy grids.
glance.problem: Goal: estimate planar pose and a global occupancy grid from noisy LiDAR while respecting SE(2) kinematics. Challenge: map and localization are coupled, so the measurement model and weight updates must be stable across long sequences.
glance.approach: I implemented grid discretization, SE(2) motion composition with Gaussian noise, LiDAR-to-world transforms, log-domain weight updates, and stratified resampling triggered by effective sample size. The map is updated in log-odds using the MAP particle.
glance.results: The pipeline yields consistent trajectories and clean occupancy maps on KITTI sequences 00-03, with stable weights and resampling only when particle diversity drops. The main gains came from careful frame transforms and log-sum-exp normalization.
takeaways: Rao-Blackwellization simplifies SLAM by factoring pose and map updates.
Numerically stable weight updates are critical for long LiDAR sequences.
Stratified resampling plus ESS thresholding keeps particles diverse.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: This project implements a Rao-Blackwellized particle filter SLAM pipeline for KITTI sequences as part of ESE 6500 at Penn.

State is a planar pose $\mathbf{x}_t = [x_t, z_t, \psi_t]^\top$ with an occupancy grid stored in log-odds. Each SLAM step consists of motion propagation, LiDAR-based observation scoring, weight normalization, and map updates using the MAP particle.
The emphasis is on theory-meets-implementation: consistent SE(2) operations, robust grid discretization, and numerically stable inference for long sequences.

sections.title: Implementation Details (Particle Filter SLAM)
paragraphs: I follow the SLAM loop from motion to sensing to mapping, keeping the math explicit so each step matches a concrete implementation block.

Motion model: ground-truth KITTI poses are converted to $[x, z, \psi]$, and control inputs are extracted via a group-consistent operator, $$\mathbf{u}_t = \mathbf{x}_t \ominus \mathbf{x}_{t-1}.$$ Each particle propagates with $$\mathbf{x}_t^{(i)} = \mathbf{x}_{t-1}^{(i)} \oplus (\mathbf{u}_t + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}), \quad \boldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{Q}),$$ using smart_plus_2d for consistent SE(2) composition and angle wrapping.

LiDAR to world: points are lifted to homogeneous coordinates, transformed by the Velodyne-to-camera extrinsics, projected to the ground plane, and transformed by each particle's SE(2) pose, $$\mathbf{T}(\psi, \mathbf{t}) = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\psi & -\sin\psi & t_x \\ \sin\psi & \cos\psi & t_z \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}.$$ This yields particle-conditioned point clouds for scoring and map updates.

Grid discretization: continuous $(x, z)$ is mapped to cell indices and clamped to map bounds, $$i = \left\lfloor \frac{x - x_{\min}}{\Delta} \right\rfloor, \quad j = \left\lfloor \frac{z - z_{\min}}{\Delta} \right\rfloor, \quad (i, j) \in [0, s_x-1] \times [0, s_z-1].$$ This produces a stacked integer index array for vectorized occupancy updates.

Log-domain weight update: observation log-likelihoods $\ell_i = \log p(\mathbf{y}_t \mid \mathbf{x}_t^{(i)})$ are normalized with log-sum-exp, then weights are updated via $$\tilde{w}_i = w_i \exp\bigl(\ell_i - \mathrm{LSE}(\boldsymbol{\ell})\bigr), \quad w_i \leftarrow \frac{\tilde{w}_i}{\sum_j \tilde{w}_j}.$$ This avoids underflow when likelihoods vary sharply.

Observation + map update: LiDAR points are discretized into occupied cells, particle scores reflect overlap with the binarized map, and the MAP particle updates the log-odds grid with occupied and free-space increments plus clipping, $$L_t(m) \leftarrow \mathrm{clip}\big(L_{t-1}(m) + \Delta L_{\text{occ/free}}\big).$$ A binarized buffer is maintained for fast scoring.

Stratified resampling: with normalized weights $\{w_i\}_{i=1}^N$, I draw $r \sim \mathcal{U}(0, 1/N)$ and build thresholds $$u_m = r + \frac{m}{N}, \quad m=0,\dots,N-1,$$ then walk the CDF to choose ancestors. Resampling resets weights to $1/N$ and is triggered only when $$N_{\text{eff}} = \frac{1}{\sum_i w_i^2}$$ drops below a fixed ratio.

sections.title: Results
paragraphs: The final occupancy grids and trajectories are consistent across KITTI sequences 00-03, with stable pose estimates and clean map structure over long horizons.

sections.title: Notes on Contribution
paragraphs: My contribution was the full SLAM pipeline: particle initialization, dynamics propagation, observation likelihoods, weight updates, stratified resampling, and log-odds map updates.
The approach follows standard particle-filter SLAM structure, but performance hinges on clean frame transforms, stable weight normalization, and careful handling of grid bounds.
